headline_marked: [[Leaked DLSS 5 runs in Control]] with early Blackwell test dropping RTX 5070 Ti from 71 to 35 FPS at 4K
headline: Leaked DLSS 5 runs in Control with early Blackwell test dropping RTX 5070 Ti from 71 to 35 FPS at 4K
summary: Modders have successfully enabled a leaked version of Nvidia's upcoming DLSS 5 neural rendering in the game Control. Early tests on an RTX 5070 Ti at 4K reportedly saw performance drop from 71 FPS to 35 FPS, though this is an unoptimized implementation.
details: A new Nvidia library, nvngx_dlssnr.dll, believed to be DLSS 5 neural rendering, was found in NBA 2K27's early access. Modders quickly got this leaked version running in the game Control. This early test is the first public glimpse of the technology.

DLSS 5 is Nvidia's next-generation neural rendering technology, first announced in March. It is expected to officially launch this fall. The current leak provides an unofficial preview of its capabilities.

Developers behind RenoDX, a game modding toolset, successfully injected DLSS 5 into Control, applying it to character models. The implementation offers seven different styles with adjustable parameters like intensity and tone.

Early performance tests on an RTX 5070 Ti at 4K reportedly showed a significant framerate drop from 71 FPS to 35 FPS with DLSS 5 enabled. The modders noted that this early version currently runs only on Blackwell GPUs.

It's crucial to remember this is an unoptimized, early implementation by modders. The performance and hardware compatibility are not representative of the final official release. Nvidia has been working on optimizing the model for single-GPU use.

Despite the early stage, image quality comparisons in Control show impressive improvements. Enhanced shadows and light transmission through hair and skin create more photorealistic scenes without altering the game's original geometry or artistic style.

headline_marked: [[AI Agent Phones]] are smartphones an LLM-powered agent can operate autonomously
headline: AI Agent Phones are smartphones an LLM-powered agent can operate autonomously
summary: These devices allow AI agents to see the screen, tap, swipe, and type, completing multi-step tasks directly within native apps, unlike API-based automation.
details: An AI agent phone is a real or cloud-hosted smartphone that an LLM-powered agent can operate on its own. It interacts with the device by seeing the screen, tapping, swiping, typing, and opening apps, completing multi-step tasks just like a person would.

Unlike calling an API, the agent uses the phone directly, operating the same Instagram, banking, or delivery apps a human would, driven by a model instead of a thumb. This concept differs from products that merely sell phone numbers for AI agents to handle voice and SMS.

Most agent tooling currently exists in browsers or desktop environments, missing the mobile-first reality where a significant share of real workflows are app-only. This includes ride-hailing, food delivery, mobile banking, two-factor prompts, and creator tools.

A browser agent cannot install an APK, respond to push notifications, read an SMS one-time code, use the camera, or drive native apps without web builds. A phone agent can. This also ensures higher fidelity, as the agent automates the actual customer experience, not a mock or internal endpoint.

A mobile AI agent operates using a perception-decision-action (PDA) loop. It builds understanding from the accessibility tree, which provides structured, machine-readable on-screen elements, and vision, using a screenshot passed to a multimodal model for visual context.

The agent receives a natural language goal, reasons about the current screen, selects the next action (tap, type, swipe, back, launch), and executes it. The screen changes, and the loop repeats until the task is complete or the agent encounters an issue.

It's not without limitations; agents can get stuck on unfamiliar screens, misread layouts, or stall on captchas and complex login walls. Long multi-step tasks can drift, and the see-think-act loop introduces latency, making agents slower than hardcoded scripts.

Mobilerun is an open-source framework enabling natural-language control of Android and iOS devices, both real and virtual, often in parallel. It can be installed locally or accessed via a hosted beta, allowing users to interact with an agent and observe phone actions.
